## 1. Purpose, scope and roles

Agree what the management system covers, whose needs matter, and which obligations need competent determination. The output is a reviewed boundary and an honest issues list, not an assertion that every obligation has been found.

Process identity: **P01**. Accountable process owner: **IMS implementation manager**.
The roles in the table perform the work. Actual appointments and deputies must be
recorded before adoption; fictional names in the example are not appointments.
This is an administrative IMS workflow, not permission to operate, isolate, repair
or restart chemical equipment.

## 2. Trigger and prerequisites

**Trigger:** Start of implementation; new site, product, customer, provider, obligation or material internal/external change; planned context review.

**Required inputs/resources:** Site/process inventory, organizational chart, customer commitments, worker input, external-provider interfaces and available obligation sources. Obtain access and time from a management sponsor; do not invent missing legal or technical conclusions.

## 3. Process map and controlled steps

Inventory actual work → hear interested parties → identify needs and obligations → propose boundary → challenge exclusions → management decision → communicate and review

Use the [worksheet](ORR-FRM-CTX-001_DEFINE-CONTEXT-AND-SCOPE-WORKSHEET.md). Each row below is a discrete proposed control:
who and when are explicit; the action/method and acceptance test are in the step;
where is the scoped process and its authorized private record store; why is the
purpose above, refined to the linked objective/risk in each execution record.
Copy each adopted control into the risk/control register with its own stable ID.

| Step | Performer | Trigger/frequency | Action and method/criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Implementation manager | At initiation and each material change | List sites, products/services, activities, outsourced steps and dependencies; interview workers and process owners. Include shifts and abnormal work, not only organizational departments. | Context worksheet; interview/source references and unresolved questions. |
| 2 | Process owner with worker/customer representatives | Before proposing scope | Record parties, their needs and the evidence source. Distinguish preference, contract commitment and potentially applicable legal duty. Assign a competent obligation assessor for uncertain duties. | Party/need entries with obligation status and assessor. |
| 3 | Implementation manager | Before management decision | Draft organizational and physical boundaries, interfaces and applicability reasons. Challenge exclusions against actual work and commitments; document impacts on quality, environment, OH&S and continuity. | Scope statement, interface list and exclusion rationale. |
| 4 | Management sponsor | At scope decision and after material boundary changes | Review unresolved material items with competent advisers. Accept only a clearly bounded scope and resource the open assessments; do not approve a compliance claim while applicability is unknown. | Dated decision identifying exact worksheet version, conditions, owners and due dates. |
| 5 | Implementation manager | After decision; at agreed review date or change trigger | Brief affected owners, pass risks to P04 and legal/environmental/OH&S/continuity inputs to their receiving processes. Track acknowledgment and review triggers. | Distribution evidence and linked risk/action IDs. |

## 4. Acceptance, holds and escalation

A reviewer can identify the boundary, each material interface, evidence for party needs, unresolved obligations and accountable follow-up. Scope agreement is separate from proving conformity.

If an exclusion conceals actual work or a material obligation is unresolved, hold the affected scope/compliance claim. Escalate to the sponsor and competent assessor with a due date; keep unaffected fact gathering moving. Urgent unsafe conditions use the site response route immediately, not this worksheet.

Measure overdue decisions/actions, missing mandatory evidence and failed control
executions in this process; define population and review interval locally. Do not
interpret “no reports” as “no problems.” Review both performance and reporting access.

## 5. Outputs, interfaces and records

Send scope/context decisions to risk owners; risk decisions to objective/control
owners; changed methods/forms to document control; performance and unresolved
issues to management review. The receiving owner acknowledges the handoff.
Record the incoming ID, outgoing ID, sender, receiver and acceptance or rejection.
Use one authoritative operational index for completed worksheets and evidence;
retain original event identity and template revision. The public examples are not
that operational index. The worksheet defines fields and filing rules.

## 6. Configure and test before use

Replace organizational placeholders; confirm scope, actual roles, lawful obligations,
approval limits, response times, retention/access and dependencies. Have relevant
specialists verify technical criteria. Execute one normal case and one held or
failed case with intended users; record findings before approval. Use
[the shared acceptance protocol](ORR-ASP-IMP-001_BEGINNER-KIT-ACCEPTANCE.md).

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.
